reader.summary: The week was dominated by the approaching October 27 Israeli election and a major escalation in the West Bank. Two Israeli soldiers were killed in a shooting attack near Hebron, prompting Prime Minister Netanyahu to order a full closure of the West Bank, launch what he called a large-scale anti-terror operation, and begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in the city. The campaign between Netanyahu and his main challenger, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, turned increasingly ugly, with extreme rhetoric from both sides and the far-right Ben-Gvir seeking new ground among young voters. Arab parties positioned themselves as kingmakers, while Israelis abroad traveled home in large numbers to vote. Trump endorsed Netanyahu nine days before the vote, while Vice President JD Vance notably declined to do so. Settler violence surged, with masked settlers attacking European diplomats, a French mayor, and a US journalist, and the Israeli military detaining US congressional candidate Brad Lander at an olive harvest. Israel arrested ten suspects over the attacks. In Gaza, the World Food Programme cut aid to 500,000 Palestinians over funding shortages, and Israeli fire killed at least four. Israel also pushed to restart strikes against Iran, and Defense Secretary Hegseth made an unannounced visit to discuss the matter.

display.eli5:
Israel is going to the polls on Tuesday, October 27, to decide whether Benjamin Netanyahu stays as prime minister or whether his challenger Gadi Eisenkot takes over. At the same time, the army is running a big operation in the West Bank after two soldiers were killed near Hebron, and in Gaza, the UN food agency is cutting its rations because it is short of money.

Netanyahu has been in power for a long time and his critics say he has weakened the courts and the military. Eisenkot is a former army chief who promises a tougher but different approach. The race is so close that small parties, including the Arab lists and the far-right Ben-Gvir, will probably decide who gets to form a government.

Next week, the biggest story will be the election result and the scramble to build a coalition. In the West Bank, the military operation will keep expanding with more buildings knocked down and more people detained. In Gaza, the food cut will start to show up in longer queues and more reports of hungry children.

A surprise would be a big attack on Israel right around election day, or a sudden agreement between Eisenkot and the far right that nobody expected. Either would change the whole political picture in a matter of hours.

history_used.HISTORY_BULLETINS:
Round 2026-10-22:
Israel stood on the brink of a tightly contested general election scheduled for October 27, pitting Prime Minister Netanyahu against former Defense Minister Gadi Eisenkot in a race where no side appeared close to a clean 61-seat mandate. In Gaza, commercial goods had been briefly suspended over a merchant-Hamas tax dispute before Israel announced their return, while the World Food Programme cut its beneficiary count from 1.6 million to 1.1 million, raising winter-shock fears. The West Bank saw a sharp spike in settler violence during the olive harvest, including attacks on European diplomats, a U.S. journalist, and a U.S. congressional candidate; Israel arrested ten suspects. On the diplomatic front, the United States and Israel advanced joint strike planning against Iran, with Secretary Hegseth making an unannounced visit to Jerusalem, while Trump openly endorsed Netanyahu and Vice President Vance withheld his. Large numbers of diaspora Israelis were flying home to vote.
- October 27 election (dominant, escalating): Netanyahu and Eisenkot face each other in a razor-thin race where neither side appears close to 61 seats.
- Gaza commercial goods (dominant, de-escalating): Commercial shipments were suspended over a tax dispute and Israel announced their partial resumption.

- West Bank settler violence (dominant, escalating): Settlers attacked harvesters, diplomats, and a U.S. journalist during the olive season; Israel arrested ten.
- Iran-U.S. strike planning (regular, escalating): Washington and Jerusalem advanced joint military planning for Iran with the actual operation targeted after U.S. midterms.
- Trump endorsement (regular, new): Trump gave Netanyahu a full public endorsement while Vance stayed silent, splitting the U.S. Jewish vote.
- Diaspora voting surge (regular, new): Large numbers of Israelis abroad flew home to vote, many motivated to challenge Netanyahu.
- Far-right fragmentation (regular, escalating): Ben-Gvir, Ofer Winter, and other challengers split the anti-Netanyahu right and complicate coalition building.
- Economic markets (occasional, continuing): The Central Bank held rates steady and raised growth forecasts, but bonds and the shekel stayed nervous.
